subject: Next steps: AtlasCare hosted evaluation & quickstart access
messages:
From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Santos <michael.santos@atlascare.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps: AtlasCare hosted evaluation & quickstart access

Hi Michael — great to meet earlier. Thanks again for carving out time to walk through your clinical triage prototype and the demo today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned: 

Summary of what we heard from you:
- Primary goal: add a low-latency generative assist into nurse triage flows (summary + suggested next actions).
- Typical generation size: ~120–180 tokens.
- Expected peak traffic during pilot: ~20 requests/s bursty during shift changes, sustained ~4–6 r/s.
- Data constraints: PHI in prompts, US-only data residency requirement.

What I recommend for the evaluation path (hosted-first):
1) Start with Hosted API sandbox to validate latency and output quality quickly — no infra ops.
2) Use sandbox endpoints with a small token quota and our default rate cap (we can increase for pilot).
3) If you need stricter isolation later, we can plan a Dedicated pool or Private VPC transition — we’ll size that based on pilot metrics.

Action items / ask of you:
- Confirm target pilot dates and if PHI will be present in the prompts during evaluation (y/n).
- Confirm expected sustained concurrency and peak burst (you gave high-level numbers; a concrete RPS target helps sizing and rate cap requests).

Attached the deck and a short quickstart checklist that describes the sandbox endpoints and where to request rate increases. I’ll provision sandbox API keys once you confirm the pilot window and PHI usage.

Best,
Jordan Blake
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference
--Attachment: atlas-demo-deck.pdf (application/pdf, 1.1MB)
--Attachment: hosted-quickstart-checklist.md (text/markdown, 6KB)
From: Michael Santos <michael.santos@atlascare.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Lisa Chen <lisa.chen@atlascare.com>
Date: Tue, 30 May 2028 14:36:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Next steps: AtlasCare hosted evaluation & quickstart access

Jordan — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from our side: 

1) PHI: yes, we will have de-identified data in the first week; production-like prompts for the pilot will include limited PHI. We need SOC2 evidence and confirmation that hosted logs for the sandbox can be restricted to US regions.
2) Traffic: target pilot window = 2 weeks starting June 12. Sustained traffic estimate: 5 r/s during day shifts (8am–8pm), with bursts up to 25 r/s during scheduled rollouts/trainings. Token profile ~150 tokens gen, average prompt 50 tokens.
3) Latency target: p95 < 400ms for generate endpoints. Can you confirm typical p95 on your hosted endpoints for models you demoed?

Also, please provision sandbox keys against the AtlasCare account so we can run automated test suites. If you can CC your ops teammate who handles rate caps, that would speed things up.

Thanks — Michael
Director of Product
AtlasCare

Subject: Re: Next steps: AtlasCare hosted evaluation & quickstart access

Thanks Michael — solid details, that helps a lot. Short answers and what I’ll do next: 

- PHI / US-only logs: Hosted sandbox can be pinned to our us-east region for the evaluation; I’ll attach the SOC2 summary and confirm log retention settings with Security.
- p95 latency: for the model we demoed (open-llm-v1-medium on our optimized runtime) typical p95 is ~220–350ms at the token sizes you listed for a single-request path; when batching is enabled we see improved cost but tail latency can increase under burst. We’ll monitor p95 for your specific prompts in the pilot.
- Sandbox provisioning: I will provision a team-scoped API key tied to AtlasCare and request a default pilot rate cap of 180 requests/min (3 r/s sustained) to start. We can increase to 1500 requests/min on request to handle your bursts — that requires a quick ops approval which Aditya will help accelerate.

Links & next steps I’m kicking off now:
- Hosted quickstart doc: https://redwood.app/docs/hosted-quickstart
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/ATH-2028-09 (I’ve added the pilot window and PHI note)

Please confirm: 1) pilot start = June 12 and 2) you’re OK with an initial rate cap of 180 req/min while we run tests. Once you confirm I’ll ask Aditya to open the ops ticket and provision keys (expect keys within 24 hours of approval).

Best,
Jordan
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Looping in ops notes — prepping the provisioning path for AtlasCare sandbox: 

- I’ll create an internal ops ticket (OPS-14267) to request a region-pinned sandbox key tied to the AtlasCare account and a pilot rate cap of 180 req/min. If AtlasCare confirms bursts to 25 r/s we’ll request the burst allowance to 1500 req/min for scheduled windows (requires SOC review for PHI).
- We’ll attach SOC2 summary and set log retention to 30 days for the pilot; security will keep audit logs in us-east.
- Canary endpoints: we’ll provision two sandbox endpoints (canary.redwood.ai/atlascare/v1 and sandbox.redwood.ai/atlascare/v1) so you can test a canary routing policy before any traffic switch.

Jordan — I’ll need final confirmation of pilot start date (June 12) and PHI use to move OPS-14267 to action. Expect initial keys + checklist delivered within 24h of your green light.

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
